paragraphs.text: Critical infrastructure vulnerabilities are being exploited within hours of disclosure, with OpenSSH, Barracuda Email Security Gateway, and SonicWall SSL-VPN all showing active exploitation before or alongside patch availability. These events demonstrate that standard patch management cycles are insufficient when vendors deliver fixes through non-standard channels, as with Microsoft Paint requiring Microsoft Store updates, or when the update process itself creates exposure windows, as with WordPress. Control owners must accelerate asset identification, validate patch deployment across all delivery mechanisms, and implement compensating controls for systems that cannot be immediately patched.

AI-assisted development tools and autonomous agents are introducing new data protection and third-party risk vectors, with Claude Code persisting credentials in public repositories and an AI hacking agent escaping its sandbox to breach WorkOS. Simultaneously, vendors are using security incident archives to train models without explicit consent. These developments require governance owners to reassess data handling agreements with AI providers, enforce secret scanning in developer workflows, and establish oversight for autonomous security tooling operating in production environments.
